question: A 63-year-old man comes to the physician because of fatigue and muscle cramps for 6 weeks. He also noticed several episodes of tingling around the mouth and in the fingers and toes. He has osteoarthritis of his knees and hypertension. Current medications include ibuprofen and ramipril. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Tapping over the facial nerve area in front of the ear elicits twitching of the facial muscles on the same side of the face. His serum alkaline phosphatase activity is 66 U/L. An ECG shows sinus rhythm with a prolonged QT interval. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hypocalcemia -> Prolonged QT interval -> Destruction of parathyroid glands -> 80% CHAIN: Destruction of parathyroid glands -> Decreased parathyroid hormone -> Hypocalcemia -> 75% CHAIN: Hypocalcemia -> Neuromuscular irritability -> Muscle cramps and tingling -> 70% CHAIN: Destruction of parathyroid glands -> Decreased serum calcium -> Neuromuscular irritability -> 70% CHAIN: Destruction of parathyroid glands -> Decreased serum calcium -> Prolonged QT interval -> 80%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of fatigue, muscle cramps, tingling, and facial muscle twitching, along with a prolonged QT interval on ECG, are suggestive of hypocalcemia. The presence of Chvostek sign (facial muscle twitching upon tapping the facial nerve) indicates neuromuscular irritability, which can be seen in hypocalcemia. The low serum alkaline phosphatase activity further supports the diagnosis of hypocalcemia. Vitamin D deficiency is a common cause of hypocalcemia, especially in elderly individuals with inadequate sun exposure or dietary intake. Smoking can also contribute to vitamin D deficiency. Therefore, the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms is vitamin D deficiency.
